content:
"The search for Vijaya Lakshmi Gali, an Indian visitor who fell into a deep sinkhole in Kuala Lumpur, has been paused because rescuers judged further action too hazardous. She vanished after the pavement gave way beneath her while she was walking along a road on 23 August, and only her slippers have been recovered so far.

Emergency teams have used tracker dogs, remote cameras, and ground-penetrating radar in hopes of finding her, but no sign of her has been discovered. The rescue effort has also involved flushing sections of the underground flood channel with powerful water streams and clearing rubble with heavy machinery.

* Officials said the danger to rescue staff was the main reason for stopping the search, and two divers who entered earlier on Thursday were pulled back before reaching the obstruction. Authorities also noted that a soil slip had been reported at the same spot last year, raising further concern about stability.

The pause in the search highlights how unstable and dangerous the area remains, even as teams continue to look for answers. The incident has drawn attention to the risks faced by rescuers working in difficult urban collapse scenes, where hidden cavities can threaten both victims and those attempting to help.

For now, the effort remains on hold while authorities weigh safety against the chance of finding her. The case has become a stark reminder of how suddenly a routine walk can turn into a tragic emergency in a busy city. Is there anything else I can help with?"
